findings.checklist_item: Specify how the per-component markers coexist with the global up-to-date gate (autodeploy.sh:474) and the global `deployed-sha` footer stamp (:763): either retire the global marker in favour of the two component markers, or state that the footer's incompleteness guard suppresses the global stamp AND that the top-level up-to-date exit is re-pointed/removed so a component skipped-with-delta is still reached next tick.
evidence: autodeploy.sh:474 `if [ "$TARGET" = "$DEPLOYED" ]; then rm -f "$DEFER_FILE"; ... log "up to date"; exit 0`
autodeploy.sh:763 `echo "$TARGET" > "$SHA_FILE.tmp" && mv "$SHA_FILE.tmp" "$SHA_FILE"` -- the single global stamp

Plan: 'each component's delta gate RE-POINTED to diff from its own marker rather than the global $DEPLOYED baseline' -- speaks only to the per-component delta gates, not the top-level global up-to-date gate that exits the whole tick first

ABSENCE: the plan's incompleteness flags 'honoured by the footer guard' do not specify whether the guard also suppresses the GLOBAL deployed-sha stamp, nor whether the global marker is retired entirely
findings.finding: The plan re-points each component's delta gate to its own marker but never addresses the GLOBAL up-to-date short-circuit (autodeploy.sh:474, `if [ "$TARGET" = "$DEPLOYED" ]; then ... exit 0`) which runs before either component block, nor what the footer's global `deployed-sha` stamp (line 763) becomes. If the global marker advances while a component was skipped, line 474 short-circuits the next tick and the skipped component never redeploys -- re-introducing the permanent-drop the plan fixes, via the global gate.
findings.location: Plan §'Shape of the fix' (delta-gate re-pointing) and 'Incompleteness' bullet; autodeploy.sh:474 (global up-to-date gate) and :763 (global footer stamp)
scenarios: mcp in backoff (skipped) while bot deploys on tick N: if global deployed-sha advances to TARGET, tick N+1 hits line 474 (TARGET==DEPLOYED), logs 'up to date', exits, and the pending mcp change is dropped permanently -- the exact bug the Incompleteness section targets
A tick where TARGET==global-DEPLOYED but a component marker still lags: line 474 exits before the component block can notice its own pending delta
findings.suggested_fix: Add a bullet stating the global up-to-date gate and footer stamp are replaced by per-component checks: the top-level `TARGET == DEPLOYED` exit becomes a per-component 'both markers current' check (or is removed so each component's own re-pointed delta gate decides), and the footer stamps each component marker only when that component completed and is not flagged incomplete -- there is no longer a single global `deployed-sha` write that can outrun a skipped component.

evidence: Plan defines when each is written ('written the moment that component completes') and consumers (delta gates, footer guard), but says nothing about tick concurrency or atomic write.
T9 requires update concurrency/ownership to be clear and mutation to be atomic (no TOCTOU).
findings.finding: The plan specifies CREATE and CONSUME for the new state files (per-component deployed-sha markers, mcp-deploy-backoff, incompleteness flags) but never states update-concurrency/ownership: whether two autodeploy ticks can overlap and race on writing these markers, and whether marker writes are atomic. findings.finding: The plan changes the on-disk state contract of a live deploy script (from one global deployed-sha to per-component markers plus a new backoff file) but specifies no rollback/coexistence path. If the new script is reverted, the old script reads the stale global deployed-sha and ignores the per-component markers, which can trigger the very redeploy the change prevents; conversely the first tick of the new script must interoperate with a host that only has the old marker.
